newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA ASKS S.AFRICA TO CUT PALM OIL TARIFF.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA ASKS S.AFRICA TO CUT PALM OIL TARIFF.

text.p: Malaysia on Friday asked South Africa to consider reducing the import tariff on palm oil to at least the same level as that for soybean oil.
The request was made by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad in his discussion with visiting South African President Nelson Mandela, the national Bernama news agency reported.
South Africa currently imposes an import tariff of 400 rand per tonne on palm oil and 170 rand a tonne on soybean oil.
Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi, in briefing reporters on the discussion, said Mahathir informed Mandela about Malaysia's request.
He said Mandela could not give an immediate answer to Malaysia's request but promised to look into it.
Mandela arrived on Thursday for a five-day visit to Malaysia, the final leg of his four-nation Southeast Asian tour.
